title: fix(plugin-auth): the auth IP allow-list judges the client address the server established
body:
Fixes #24739

Clause-②: no

## What changes

The ADR-0069 D5 IP allow-list (`allowed_ip_ranges`) and the D7 login audit (`last_login_ip`) now establish a request's client address by the platform's one client-address trust rule, the rule the runtime's inbound rate limiter already used:

- `X-Forwarded-For` (its first entry), then `X-Real-IP`, count only when the stack declares `server.trustProxy`.
- Otherwise the address is the transport's peer address (`IHttpRequest.remoteAddress`).
- With ranges configured, an address that cannot be established is refused with `403 IP_NOT_ALLOWED`. That is the code and status the gate already uses for an address outside the ranges. The first such refusal logs one operator warning that names `allowed_ip_ranges` and `server.trustProxy`.
- With no ranges configured, nothing is judged. This is unchanged.
- The D7 audit stamps the address the gate judged, or no address when none could be established.

The maintainer's direction, verbatim from the card: 「登录 IP 白名单信任可伪造的 IP 头，取不到 IP 时还放行」

## How

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/client-address.ts` (new) | `resolveClientAddress`: the address half of the runtime's `resolveRateLimitKey`, moved unchanged. It is published as the dependency-free `@objectstack/plugin-auth/client-address` subpath (679 B ESM, no imports), beside `./rate-limit-storage`. |
| `packages/runtime/src/security/inbound-rate-limit.ts` | `resolveRateLimitKey` imports the rule instead of keeping its own copy. Its keys are unchanged, and the limiter's own pins are green (below). |
| `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager.ts` | A `trustProxy` option. `resolveClientAddress` / `trustsForwardedHeaders`. `isClientIpAllowed` refuses an undetermined address while ranges are set. `ipMatchesRange` compares an IPv4-mapped IPv6 address as its IPv4 address: a dual-stack socket reports IPv4 peers that way, and the gate now judges the peer. `handleRequest(request, { remoteAddress })` establishes the address once and carries it to the D7 stamp in better-auth's request state. The `allowedIpRanges` TSDoc no longer states the fail-open. |
| `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/request-client-address.ts` (new) | The request-state slot that carries the established address to the sign-in after-hook. |
| `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-plugin.ts` | The D5 middleware judges `resolveClientAddress` over the request's headers and transport peer. The wildcard route hands the same peer to `handleRequest`. Two once-per-process operator warnings. |
| `packages/cli/src/commands/serve.ts` | `objectstack serve` passes `server.trustProxy` to `AuthPlugin`, as it already does to the dispatcher. |
| `packages/services/service-settings/src/manifests/auth.manifest.ts`, `translations/{zh-CN,ja-JP,es-ES}.ts` | The `allowed_ip_ranges` help text says which address is judged. It used to say a trusted proxy setting `X-Forwarded-For` was enough. |
| `content/docs/permissions/authentication.mdx` | The `allowed_ip_ranges` row, which stated the old IP source and the fail-open. |
| `.changeset/24739-auth-ip-allowlist-trust-rule.md` | patch: plugin-auth, runtime, cli, service-settings. |

**Why the rule lives in plugin-auth.** `@objectstack/runtime` depends on `@objectstack/plugin-auth`: its limiter already counts through `./rate-limit-storage`. So plugin-auth cannot import the runtime's copy without a dependency cycle. The rule moved, and the runtime imports it back. The package root's export surface is unchanged.

**Why the peer is read from the Hono context.** The D5 gate and the route that feeds the D7 audit are raw-app mounts. They receive the Hono context, not an `IHttpRequest`. The read mirrors the transport's own `readRemoteAddress` (`plugin-hono-server/src/adapter.ts`), and returns nothing on a runtime that exposes no socket.

## Pins, one per branch

`packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/client-ip-allow-list-trust-rule.test.ts` mounts `AuthPlugin.registerAuthRoutes` on a real Hono app in front of a real `AuthManager` on the installed better-auth. It supplies the peer the way `@hono/node-server` does. Every refusal asserts `status` and `code`.

- behind a declared trusted proxy, the allow-list judges the forwarded client address
- without a declared trusted proxy, the allow-list judges the connection peer and a forwarded header changes nothing
- an address the server could not establish is refused while ranges are set, and the operator is told why once
- with no ranges configured nothing is judged, whatever the address
- an IPv4 peer reported in IPv4-mapped form is judged as its IPv4 address
- (D7) records the connection peer, not a forwarded header, when no proxy is trusted
- (D7) records the forwarded client address the gate admitted when the proxy is declared trusted
- (D7) records no address when none could be established

`auth-manager.test.ts`: the old "fails OPEN when the client IP cannot be determined" case is now "refuses an address the server could not establish once ranges are configured". Two cases are new: the IPv4-mapped matcher, and `resolveClientAddress` believing forwarded headers only under `trustProxy`.

## Ablations

Each leg was committed first and restored from `HEAD`: `git checkout HEAD -- PATH`, or `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`, which wraps the run. Each restore is proven by the blob hash matching `HEAD` and an empty `git diff HEAD`. The pins import `src` relatively, so no `dist/` is involved.

| Leg | Mutation | Red | Green |
|---|---|---|---|
| A1 | `auth-plugin.ts` + `auth-manager.ts` at base `795ff708d8` (the old behaviour) | 8: the untrusted-proxy, undetermined and IPv4-mapped pins; D7 peer; D7 none; the 3 new or flipped units | the trusted-proxy, no-ranges and D7 trusted pins. These are the preservation half: the old code believed headers too |
| A2 | `client-address.ts`: the trust branch ignored | 3: the trusted-proxy pin, D7 trusted, the unit's trusted leg | the rest |
| A3 | `isClientIpAllowed`: no ranges refuses | 4: the no-ranges pin, its unit, and the two D7 pins served with no ranges | the rest |
| A4 | the wildcard route hands no peer to `handleRequest` | 1: D7 peer | the rest |

## Cross-lane surfaces

- `packages/runtime/src/security/inbound-rate-limit.ts` (`domain:cli`): declared in the claim.
- `packages/cli/src/commands/serve.ts` (`domain:cli`): not in the claim's file surface. It is one option line, and it is what lets `server.trustProxy` reach the gate under `objectstack serve`.
- `packages/services/service-settings` (help text) and `content/docs/permissions/authentication.mdx`: text this change made false. Neither is in the claim's file surface.

## Acceptance notes

- ADR-0069 D5 names the gate's IP source as "extract client IP (`x-forwarded-for` / `cf-connecting-ip`, trust-proxy aware)". This PR implements "trust-proxy aware" as the runtime's rule, which reads `X-Forwarded-For`, then `X-Real-IP`. `CF-Connecting-IP` is no longer read. The ADR text is not edited here.
- The spec's `server.trustProxy` description names one consumer, the inbound rate limiter. This change adds a second: the auth allow-list and the login audit. `packages/spec` is not edited here.
- Other HTTP doors into `AuthManager.handleRequest` pass no transport peer. Their D7 stamp therefore records no address unless `server.trustProxy` is declared. Their D5 coverage was not measured here.
- `objectstack dev` (`plugin-dev`) composes `AuthPlugin` without `trustProxy`, the same way it composes the dispatcher without it.
- `docs/HARDENING.md` shows a hand-written limiter keyed on `x-forwarded-for`. It is unchanged here.
- Disclosure follows the maintainer's ruling recorded on #9387. This PR states the rule and its refusals only.
